Understands what you want. You : Use Tauri for this project, not Electron You : I mentioned my style before — clean and restrained Memmy: Got it all noted. No need to repeat next time. #1 REMEMBER It remembers what you said Automatically reads your local AI collaboration history and turns scattered conversations, preferences and technical decisions into structured memory. Cursor → Claude #2 RELAY Switch tools freely, memory stays online Out of Cursor credits and switching to Claude? Memmy carries your project context, preferences and progress over for you. “Merge the plans we discussed across agents into one.” “Turn this week's technical decisions into a doc.” “Remember: don't write overly sugary copy for me.” #3 ACT It's an agent itself Not just a memory manager — hand it tasks directly: organize material, merge plans, or continue what you left unfinished. How it works Three steps, from strangers to in sync 01 Scan After you authorize it, Memmy scans the conversation history of AI tools on your device, like Cursor, Claude and Codex. 02 Organize Distills scattered conversations into structured memory — your preferences, decisions, project background and pitfalls — deduplicated, categorized and searchable. 03 Inject When you switch to any AI tool, Memmy hands it the most relevant memory — not a full data dump, but precise on-demand matching. DATA SECURITY Your memory belongs to you alone 01 All memory stays local Every piece of memory data is stored on your own device and never uploaded to any remote server. Your computer is your memory vault. 02 Never collected without consent Memmy never reads or processes any AI conversation history without your knowledge. Every scan requires your explicit authorization and can be revoked at any time. 03 You decide who can use it You fully control which agent can use each memory and how much context is passed. You can view or delete any memory anytime, and turn off any source. Community Join us to make Memmy better Memmy is open source and constantly evolving. Every piece of feedback helps it understand you a little better.
